Title: Nigerians Must Obtain Tax ID To Operate Bank Accounts By 2026 - New Tax Law - Business - Nigeria

Summary: 
The Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025, signed by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, will take effect on 1 January 2026. From that date, no individual or business can open or operate a bank account, run a business, or access financial services without a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN). The law also requires all government agencies (MDAs) and foreign suppliers to obtain a TIN before entering contracts or doing business in Nigeria. Under Section 8(2), banks, insurers, and stockbrokers will be barred from providing services to anyone without a valid TIN. The reform is described as the most significant change in Nigeria’s financial and tax system in decades, aiming to widen the tax net and reduce reliance on oil. Key metrics cited in the article include Nigeria’s 10 % tax‑to‑GDP ratio compared with Ghana’s 13 %, Kenya’s 16 %, South Africa’s 27 %+, and the global average of 34 %. Out of over 200 million citizens, only 10 million are registered taxpayers, while more than 60 million Nigerians hold bank accounts. The Act also abolishes the Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) and replaces it with the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS). Public reactions quoted a civil servant in Abuja saying, 'It's good for accountability, but I fear delays and corruption in the process,' and a Lagos‑based tax consultant who welcomed the reform, stating, 'This is long overdue. Without linking tax IDs to financial services, compliance will never improve.' The article notes potential risks such as exclusion of the 38 million unbanked adults, bureaucratic delays, corruption, and an awareness gap that could create chaos at tax offices.

Published date: September 09 2025, 07:42

Source: Nairaland

Title: Active bank accounts in Nigeria rise to 320 million in March 2025 - NIBSS

Summary: 
The Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS) has reported that the number of active bank accounts in Nigeria rose to 320 million in March 2025, a 2.5% increase from the 311.6 million at the end of 2024. This represents 8.4 million new accounts opened or reactivated between January and March. According to the World Bank, access to a transaction account is a key step towards financial inclusion. However, the NIBSS data also shows that 33.3 million accounts are inactive or dormant, a 70% increase from 19.5 million at the end of 2024. Additionally, 29.4 million accounts have been closed. The number of active bank accounts still lags behind the number of Bank Verification Numbers (BVN), which is a compulsory requirement for opening an account.

Title: Active bank accounts in Nigeria hit 320m, NIBSS declares

Summary: 
The number of active bank accounts in Nigeria has reached a record 320 million as of March 2025, according to the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS). This growth is attributed to increased adoption of digital banking, mobile accounts, and fintech-driven solutions, particularly among Nigeria's youthful population and informal sector. However, questions remain about account dormancy rates, duplication across banks, and the actual percentage of financially active individuals versus registered accounts. Financial experts have called for deeper reforms to ensure that account ownership translates to real financial inclusion and economic empowerment. The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC) has also committed to reimbursing outstanding insured amounts to all eligible depositors of the failed Heritage Bank, with payments ongoing and the corporation committed to successful reimbursement. 'We apologise for the delay in your payment and any challenges you may have experienced. Kindly note that NDIC has continued to pay depositors. Payment has been ongoing, and the corporation is committed to successful reimbursement to all eligible depositors,' NDIC said.

Title: Over 60 million dormant or closed bank accounts as NIN deadline bites

Summary: 
Nigeria's banking system has seen a significant spike in account closures and dormancy, with 29.4 million accounts closed as of March 2025, according to the Nigerian Interbank Settlement System (NIBSS). This comes after the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) mandated all financial institutions to link National Identity Numbers (NIN) and Bank Verification Numbers (BVN) to all tier-1 accounts by March 1, 2024. The policy aims to improve identity verification, eliminate ghost accounts, and fight fraud. The number of inactive or dormant accounts has ballooned to 33.39 million, a 71.3% increase from March 2024. Experts warn that this could complicate the country's goal of expanding financial inclusion, especially among low-income and rural populations. Despite the closures, active bank accounts have grown significantly, reaching 320.05 million in March 2025, up 45.7% from a year earlier. 'Time is running out' for account holders yet to link their NINs, according to Legit.ng's Pascal Oparada.

Published date: July 25 2025, 19:07

Title: Nigeria Reaches 66.2M BVN-Linked Bank Accounts as Digital Banking Adoption Grows

Summary: 
Nigeria has reached 66.2 million bank account owners with linked Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs) as of July 2025, a 2.7 million increase from January 2025. The growth comes amid a broader push for digital identity verification, with the National Identity Database reaching 122 million registrations. The BVN system provides enhanced security against unauthorized account access, and a Central Bank of Nigeria mandate requiring banks to freeze accounts lacking both BVN and National Identification Number (NIN) took effect in April 2024. Total active bank accounts in Nigeria reached 320 million by March 2025, with 8.4 million new or reactivated accounts in the first quarter of 2025. Nigeria has also experienced substantial growth in cashless transactions, with ₦295 trillion in Q1 2025, compared to ₦237.11 trillion in Q1 2024. The digital transformation has been supported by the launch of new verification tools, including the NINAuth mobile application.

Published date: August 04 2025, 04:01

Title: FG Targets 95% Digital Literacy by 2030 - NITDA DG • Okay.ng

Summary: 
The National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) Director-General, Kashifu Inuwa, has set a goal of achieving 95% digital literacy across Nigeria by 2030. This is part of the administration's agenda to accelerate industrialisation, digitisation, and innovation. Inuwa stated, 'We started this journey in 2023 when President Bola Ahmed Tinubu came on board and he made it clear that economic diversification and inclusivity are part of the administration’s agenda.' The National Digital Literacy Framework (NDLF) will focus on six core competency areas, including basic, intermediate, and advanced levels. The World Bank's Better Life Report showed a significant increase in digital literacy from 44% in 2021 to 50% in 2025. UBEC Executive Secretary Hajiya Aisha Garba emphasized the importance of collaboration, saying, 'Let us align the technical vision with grassroots realities to make a lasting impact.'

Published date: July 09 2025, 15:31

Citation key: [9]
Title: Half of Nigeria lives in poverty despite reform, World Bank says

Summary: 
According to a new World Bank report released on October 9, 2025, poverty in Nigeria is projected to reach 139 million people in 2025, up from 81 million in 2019, with most of the increase occurring before 2023. Despite economic reforms introduced by President Bola Tinubu since taking office in 2023—including currency adjustments, tax reforms, and the removal of the fuel subsidy—the report notes that 'gains have yet to substantially improve Nigerians' livelihoods.' Real incomes continue to erode due to rising prices, and businesses face persistent barriers to expansion and job creation. The report, presented by World Bank senior economist Samer Matta in Abuja, projects that poverty will remain at 62% next year before beginning to decline in 2027. The World Bank forecasts modest GDP growth of 4.2% in 2025, rising to 4.4% by 2027, driven by services, while inflation is expected to gradually fall from 20.1% (annual rate in August 2025) to 15.8% by 2027. To translate reform gains into tangible benefits, the report urges the government to reduce food inflation, improve public resource allocation for development, and strengthen the social safety net.

Published date: October 09 2025, 12:48

URL: https://iol.co.za/business-report/international/2025-10-09-half-of-nigeria-lives-in-poverty-despite-reform-world-bank-says/
Source: IOL
Classification: World
Sentiment: negative
Reporting voice: Analytical
Continent: Africa

</doc>

Citation key: [10]
Title: Banks record 29.4m closed accounts, 33m inactive

Summary: 
According to the Nigerian Interbank Settlement System (NIBSS), about 29.4 million bank accounts were recorded as closed in commercial banks as of March 2025. This represents a 30.43% or 6.86 million year-on-year increase in closed bank accounts compared to March 2024. Additionally, the number of dormant or inactive bank accounts grew by 13.6 million or 71.3% YoY to 33.39 million in March 2025. However, the number of active bank accounts grew by 100.41 million or 45.7% YoY to 320.05 million in March 2025. The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) issued a directive in December 2023 to restrict tier-1 accounts without proper Biometric Verification Number (BVN) and National Identity Number (NIN) by March 1st, 2024. As of July 2025, 66.23 million Nigerians have BVN, up from 61.6 million in April 2024.

Published date: July 24 2025, 04:33

URL: https://www.vanguardngr.com/2025/07/banks-record-29-4m-closed-accounts-33m-inactive/
Source: Vanguard
